name: IL-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent in this downstate district
LaHood holds a dominant financial edge: $6.7M cash on hand vs. $230K for Nolley
Prediction markets price LaHood at roughly 96-97% to win
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending signal any competitive threat
model.rationale: The R+11 district, LaHood's roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97% Republican leave Paul Nolley without a visible path; even a Democratic-friendly national environment only trims the expected margin to about fifteen points.
model.watch: A surge of Democratic outside spending or polling showing LaHood well below majority support would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This downstate Illinois seat leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Darin LaHood enters the general election with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean is R+11, and LaHood has built a dominant war chest: $3.7 million raised and $6.7 million on hand, against roughly $230,000 for Democrat Paul Nolley. Outside groups have spent essentially nothing in the race, and prediction markets give LaHood about a 96% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings track the contest, so the outlook rests on partisanship, money, and incumbency. A national environment that has favored Democrats this cycle narrows the expected margin but does not put the seat in play. Nolley would need a district-specific shift well beyond anything in the current evidence to threaten LaHood, who is favored by roughly fifteen points.
